chunks: And from his words (peace be upon him): He said after reciting: "Engage (your) vying in exuberance"
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean by 'Al-hakum at-takathur'?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates the transition from the competitive accumulation of wealth (takathur) to the finality of death, framing it as a spiritual blindness that prevents reflection on the Hereafter. This exegesis underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on using worldly pursuits as a means to an end rather than an end in themselves, warning that material distraction leads directly to the neglect of spiritual accountability.
